description: Soot volume fraction in microgravity sooty attached coflow flames can be several times greater than in normal-gravity comparison flames, and microgravity flames are taller and wider.
scientific_phenomenon: Soot formation and flame structure in microgravity
experimental_or_computational_context: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (CLD Flame) investigation on ISS using diluted methane and ethylene flames in air coflow.
authors_interpretation: Absence of buoyant convection leads to longer residence times and enhanced soot production, as well as extended dilution limits allowing stable lifted flames at lower fuel concentrations.
limitations_and_qualifications: Preliminary results; test duration limited by constant volume chamber constraints.

description: In electric field tests (E-FIELD Flames), microgravity flames exhibit a distinct peak ion current corresponding to the most compact flame, with clear correlations between flame luminosity, combustion intensity, and ion current.
scientific_phenomenon: Electric-field effects and chemi-ionization in diffusion flames
experimental_or_computational_context: E-FIELD Flames study burning pure and diluted methane and ethylene with gas-jet and coflow configurations under electric potentials up to 10 kV.
authors_interpretation: Direct ion transport and induced ion wind modify flame shape, suppress soot generation, and stabilize highly diluted flames with weak electric fields.
limitations_and_qualifications: High field strengths resulted in corona and arc discharges.

description: Low-momentum microgravity flames (Burning Rate Emulator - BRE) can burn for minutes without airflow or flame spread, but self-extinguish in oxygen concentrations below ~25% by volume. Smaller flames burn for minutes at elevated oxygen, while larger flames self-extinguish within 1.5 minutes (ethylene) or within a minute (methane).
scientific_phenomenon: Material flammability and extinction in quiescent microgravity atmospheres
experimental_or_computational_context: BRE investigation using flat porous burner fed with gaseous fuel simulating condensed-phase fuels at elevated oxygen and reduced pressures.
reported_numerical_values: Oxygen concentration below ~25% by volume; extinction time within 1.5 minutes (ethylene) or 1 minute (methane)
authors_interpretation: Thermal feedback and extinction behavior in still atmospheres provide fundamental data on materials flammability for spacecraft fire prevention.
limitations_and_qualifications: Simulated using gaseous fuels matching properties of solid materials.

description: In Flame Design experiments, very small flames have low radiative loss and asymptotically approach steady-state behavior (lasting over 14 minutes), whereas large flames increase in size over time until extinction due to radiative heat loss, experiencing an unstable oscillatory mode before full extinction.
scientific_phenomenon: Sooting inception, flame design, and radiative extinction oscillations
experimental_or_computational_context: Flame Design normal and inverse flame tests with various concentrations of ethylene and oxygen.
reported_numerical_values: Flame duration over 14 minutes for small flames
authors_interpretation: Flame size increases with reactant flow rate and decreases with ambient oxygen concentration; radiative heat loss drives unsteadiness and extinction in large flames.
limitations_and_qualifications: Tests terminated due to operational constraints.

description: Non-premixed spherical cool flames were discovered in normal-flame CFI-G testing with n-butane after hot flames quenched due to radiative heat loss; cool flames are significantly smaller than corresponding hot flames.
experimental_or_computational_context: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G) normal and inverse flame tests of ethane, propane, and n-butane on porous burners.
authors_interpretation: Low-temperature kinetic mechanisms support quasi-steady spherical cool flames following hot flame quenching.
limitations_and_qualifications: Observed in specific alkane (n-butane) normal-flame tests.
